request.spec: Replace the string membership tier with a numeric 'membershipLevel' from 1 to 3 on creation: start at 1; add 1 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; cap at 3 (level 4 is reserved for tenure). Remove the 'membershipTier' field from the response in favour of 'membershipLevel'. This changes the existing tier behaviour, and anything that recorded the tier (such as the create audit line) must record the level instead.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Replace the string membership tier with a numeric 'membershipLevel' from 1 to 3 on creation: start at 1; add 1 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; cap at 3 (level 4 is reserved for tenure). Remove the 'membershipTier' field from the response in favour of 'membershipLevel'. This changes the existing tier behaviour, and anything that recorded the tier (such as the create audit line) must record the level instead.

agent.result_text:
I agree with the finding and addressed it. It was correct: `householdMemberCount`'s sole reader was the GOLD branch of the old `toMembershipTier`, which my change deleted, and `countHouseholdMembers` had no callers beyond the two lines feeding that field. Nothing exposed it in the response either, so the read and create paths were doing a household round-trip that no longer fed anything.

Removed as orphaned scaffolding (none of it is needed for the reserved level-4 "tenure" work, which has no code yet):

- **`Owner.java`** — the `@Transient householdMemberCount` field and its getter/setter (the getter's Javadoc, whose stated purpose I'd already gutted last change).
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — both `setHouseholdMemberCount(countHouseholdMembers(...))` calls, in `getOwner` and `addOwner`.
- **`ClinicService.java` / `ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — the now-callerless `countHouseholdMembers` method. It only used the general-purpose `ownerRepository.findAll()`, so no repository method needed removal.

Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: `membershipLevel` derives purely from email + `namesakeCount`, and the household count never influenced it after the rename. `./mvnw -o test` → BUILD SUCCESS, 1 test run, 0 failures; and a final grep confirms no remaining references to either symbol.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The membership-level logic, DTO rename, audit line, and OpenAPI update are all clean and idiomatic. But this change removed the *only* consumer of `householdMemberCount` and left the machinery that feeds it orphaned.

**Finding: `householdMemberCount` is now dead scaffolding.**

Before this change, `householdMemberCount` existed solely to derive the `GOLD` tier (`if (householdMembers >= 3) return "GOLD"`). The new `toMembershipLevel(owner)` no longer reads it, and a grep confirms there is no other reader:

- `src/main/java/.../model/Owner.java:73,162-168` — the field + getter/setter.
- `src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:105-106` (`getOwner`) and `:152-153` (`addOwner`) — both still call `owner.setHouseholdMemberCount(clinicService.countHouseholdMembers(...))`.
- `src/main/java/.../service/ClinicService.java:64` and `ClinicServiceImpl.java:282` — the `countHouseholdMembers` service method that now backs nothing.

It is not exposed in the response either (`openapi.yml` has `householdId` and `membershipLevel`, but no `householdMemberCount`). So after this diff the app computes a household member count — including a service/repository round-trip in both read and create paths — that nothing consumes.

The tell is even in this diff: the author edited `Owner.getHouseholdMemberCount()`'s Javadoc to delete "used to derive the membership tier," leaving it as "Not persisted." — i.e. a field whose stated reason for existing was just removed, but whose population code was left behind. A maintainer landing here would be puzzled why household members are counted at all.

**Requested:** as part of retiring the tier behaviour, remove the now-unused `householdMemberCount` field/getter/setter on `Owner`, the two `setHouseholdMemberCount(...)` calls in the controller, and (if it has no other callers) the `countHouseholdMembers` method on `ClinicService`/`ClinicServiceImpl`. If any of these are intentionally being kept for the reserved "tenure" level-4 work, add a brief comment saying so — otherwise they read as orphaned code.
